newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crude firms while local trade idles.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crude firms while local trade idles.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast light crude oil gained slightly with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Wednesday, but overall spot trade remained idle as traders waited for next week's pipeline apportionment.
The local discount for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude -- the regional benchmark -- remained at $2.16 under August spot prices for West Texas Intermediate (WTI).
Refinery traders claimed to be finished buying crude for August, and waited for the start of September business.
Key seller BP continued to offer at $1.85 under August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI).

Outright prices for ANS crude rose to $17.39/17.54 a barrel, 38 cents over Tuesday. Meanwhile, Kern River grade remained 10 to 20 cents over postings. Wilmington crude, pumped from Long Beach, Calif., stood 65 to 75 cents over posting, unchanged for over a month.
Light grade Line 63 crude remained unchanged at $3.05 under WTI and about $1.00 over Buena Vista crude.
